tip: Day words take no particle: 어제 뭐 했어요? (eoje mwo haesseoyo = what did you do yesterday?) – but parts of the day do: 아침에 (achime = in the morning).
있다 (itda = to be somewhere) takes 에 (e), not 에서 (eseo): 집에 있었어요 (jibe isseosseoyo = I was at home).
저녁 (jeonyeok) means both evening and dinner: 저녁을 안 먹었어요 (jeonyeogeul an meogeosseoyo = didn't eat dinner) – 점심 (jeomsim) likewise covers midday and lunch.
에서 (eseo) marks where an action happens: 식당에서 비빔밥을 먹었어요 (sikdangeseo bibimbabeul meogeosseoyo = ate bibimbap at a restaurant) – 에 (e) would mark a destination instead.
랑 (rang) is the casual spoken 'with': 친구랑 (chingurang = with a friend). In writing or formal speech, 하고 (hago) or 와/과 (wa/gwa) fit better.
못 (mot) = couldn't, 안 (an) = chose not to: 못 샀어요 (mot sasseoyo = couldn't buy it). With 안 it would mean you decided against it.
'There was' needs only one verb: 회의가 있었어요 (hoeuiga isseosseoyo = there was a meeting) – 있다 (itda) also covers 'had', as in 'I had a meeting'.
안 (an = not) sits right before the verb: 회사에 안 갔어요 (hoesae an gasseoyo = didn't go to work) – never at the front like English 'didn't'.
로 (ro) marks the means: 비행기로 갔어요 (bihaenggiro gasseoyo = went by plane). After most consonants it becomes 으로 (euro).
No 's needed: 할머니 집 (halmeoni jip = Grandma's house) – Korean stacks the nouns and the possessive 의 (ui) usually drops out.
동생 (dongsaeng) is any younger sibling – no gender. Add 여 (yeo) or 남 (nam) only when it matters: 여동생 (yeodongsaeng) = younger sister.
전화하다 (jeonhwahada = to call) takes 한테 (hante), not 을/를 (eul/reul): 엄마한테 전화했어요 (eommahante jeonhwahaesseoyo = called my mom).
No 'to me' needed: 선물을 줬어요 (seonmureul jwosseoyo = gave me a present) – with 주다 (juda = give), an unmentioned receiver is understood as the speaker.
병원에 갔어요 (byeongwone gasseoyo) usually means seeing a doctor – Koreans say 병원 (byeongwon = hospital) for any clinic visit, however minor.
자다 (jada) covers both 'sleep' and 'go to bed': 일찍 잤어요 (iljjik jasseoyo) = went to bed early, not only 'slept early'.
시간 (sigan) counts hours of duration, 시 (si) tells clock time: 열 시간 잤어요 (yeol sigan jasseoyo = slept ten hours) – 열 시 (yeol si) is 10 o'clock.
다 (da = all) goes before the verb, not the noun: 숙제를 다 했어요 (sukjereul da haesseoyo) – literally 'homework, all did'.
